summary: The bad() method reads an arbitrary string from a TCP socket and passes it directly to Class.forName()/newInstance(), allowing an attacker to instantiate any class on the classpath (CWE-470 Unsafe Reflection). The fix validates the socket-supplied name against an allow-list of known-safe class names before reflecting on it, preserving the legitimate feature for those inputs while rejecting untrusted class names.
